reviews.review:
Game isn't perfect but it's worth it, especially if you get it on sale.  There are some weird "dead" zones with nothing in them, empty, between some fight encounters, almost like the devs had more plans for the level design.  As for the levels, there are some cool set pieces and the aesthetic is pretty.  The story is fun and entertaining.  It trucks right along at a decent pace.

As for the cons, the AI of your teammates is stupid.  They can't hit anything and are only there to offer up some dialogue throughout all the walking around for the most part.  They get in the way, block you while your fighting / rolling / dodging around, and especially when grenades get tossed your way.  Coupled with the terrain hitboxes tripping you and hanging you up on every dumb little block 4 inches high this can get pretty tedious.

The only way to heal yourself is by performing nuDoom styled executions in melee combat, but the issue is you need to whittle down most enemies with at least one hit (more at later levels) before you can attempt to stun them and then execute them.  At later levels you end up desperate through some sequences with a complete lack of fodder to execute for health.  There are definitely some fights that will make you want to pull your hair out and break a controller.

The enemy AI can get repetitive and certain ones can seem pretty unfair, being that your teammates are useless.  If you start fighting anyone in a room all the enemies will aggro onto you and ignore your teammates so they aren't even good for that.

The worst part of the game?

Elevators.  There are so many stupid elevators in this game that if you were to play the drinking game where you take a shot every time you have to ride an elevator you'd die.

The game is probably easier on a controller but I muddled my way through it with mouse and keyboard on Normal difficulty.  You could tell that the people who made the game probably play Warhammer in real life, since the levels, encounters, story, and set pieces all seemed like they were pulled from random tabletop campaigns from the past.  It's fun even if you've never played Warhammer, like me.

Space Marine is actually really fun, while the gameplay is mostly a mix of vertical and direct shooting it also has melee (good for large groups), you get the full scale of war on a planet that is truly devastated by an invasion. The melee is awesome at best but meh for the majority of it. Fits with actual warhammer lore really well and I wish it involved more planets and was longer, much more open. It's a really well rounded experience with a mid tier story to boot. But you are mainly there just to annihilate all in your path and crush heresy. The selection of weapons was neat but never found myself straying from the bolter rifle, the sheer number of orks is decent and lags sometimes even on a GTX 10603GB and Ryzen 5 2600k processor. Overall amazing game and the final boss makes it a solid 10/10
This video game breeds testosterone on emperor-class levels
